117620.name: Chabad House Center of Kansas City
117620.note: JTA Daily Bulletin (6 Jan 1970): 'Markos L'Inyonei Chinuch ... has opened its eighth regional office in the United States at Kansas City, Mo. The new office, which will serve the states of Missouri and Kansas, is headed by Rabbi Sholem B. Wineberg, 24'. The Kansas City Jewish Chronicle (CrownHeights.info, 10 Oct 2010, 'Kansas City Chabad Turns 40'): dispatched 'in 1970'; Blumah Wineberg and her husband 'founded the local Chabad House in 1970'; Rabbi Mendy Wineberg recalls 'the old Chabad House on Holmes'. Now 6201 Indian Creek Drive, Overland Park (since when not found).

earlier.where: the old Chabad House on Holmes (Road), Kansas City, Mo.

117648.name: Chabad of Greater St. Louis Regional Headquarters
117648.note: St. Louis Jewish Light (7 Nov 2006): Levi Landa 'was just an infant when his photo first appeared in the St. Louis Jewish Light in 1980 when his father, Rabbi Yosef Landa established Chabad in St. Louis'. Medium: the Jewish Light (16 Oct 2007, 'Chabad to celebrate 25 years in town') says 'Twenty-five years ago, Chabad of Greater St. Louis had a modest beginning — operating out of the apartment of Rabbi Yosef Landa and his wife, Shiffy' (so 1982), and a Chabad.org profile says the Landas moved to Missouri in 1981. The Morris and Ann Lazaroff Chabad Center on Delmar Boulevard was rededicated after a $1.5 million overhaul in Sept 2016 (Jewish Light, 28 Sept 2016).

118539.name: Chabad on Campus serving Washington U. in St. Louis
118539.note: Lubavitch.com (31 July 2002, 'Chabad Comes to Washington University'): Rabbi Yosef Landa recruited Rabbi Hershey and Chana Rochel Novack 'to establish a Chabad-Lubavitch center on campus'. St. Louis Jewish Light (2 Nov 2022): 'Rabbi Hershey and Chana Novack moved to St. Louis in 2002 to establish Chabad on Campus'. Jewish Light (13 July 2005): Chabad bought 7018 Forsyth, 'moving in spring 2006' from the Novacks' apartment; the renovated building was dedicated March 27 2011 (WashU Source, 22 March 2011).

169299.name: Chabad of Chesterfield
169299.note: St. Louis Jewish Light (2021): serving Chesterfield, Ballwin and Wildwood 'for the past 17 years' (so 2004); again (2 Sept 2022): 'for over 17 years'. Its chabad.org listing went up Sept 1 2004, so it existed by then. Rabbi Avi and Chana'la Rubenfeld. Its own building at 15310 Conway Road (groundbreaking Sept 14 2022, to open summer 2023); before that leased space (not dated here).

371907.name: Chabad Center for Jewish Life Serving KU & The Northeast Kansas Communities
371907.note: The Kansas City Jewish Chronicle (CrownHeights.info, 26 May 2006, 'KU gets its own Chabad House'): 'Rabbi Zalman and Nechama Tiechtel and their infant daughter, Mina, moved to Lawrence in March'; their home 'doubles as the Chabad House'. Rabbi Sholom Wineberg had been going to Lawrence 'for 12 years'. A new centre opened in 2025 (Chabad.org). Now 1203 W 19th Street.

767767.name: Chabad-Lubavitch of Midtown & Downtown Kansas City
767767.note: The Kansas City Jewish Chronicle (Rick Hellman; CrownHeights.info, 28 March 2009, 'Chabad of The Plaza Established'): 'Rabbi Yitzhak, Chana and Meir Itkin just moved to town'. Its chabad.org listing went up April 26 2009. Now 420 Nichols Road (the Plaza).

1686459.name: Chabad at MU
1686459.note: The Columbia Missourian (CrownHeights.info, 21 Nov 2011): 'A young rabbi who moved with his family this month from Brooklyn, N.Y., to Columbia' (Avremi and Channy Lapine). The Kansas City Jewish Chronicle (8 Dec 2011, 'Chabad on Campus expands to MU'): moved to Columbia 'about a month ago', into 'a rented two-story house'. In 2017 Chabad bought the house it had rented for six years (KCJC).

2850733.name: Chabad of Leawood
2850733.note: The Kansas City Jewish Chronicle (5 March 2015, 'The Shul-Chabad of Leawood opens new location this week'): 'In August of 2013, Chabad of Leawood opened at 4800 W. 135th St.' (a six-month lease, opened six days before Rosh Hashanah); the new location, 5051 W. 134th St., opened with Purim 2015. Co-directors Rabbi Mendy and Devory Wineberg, 'joined soon' by Rabbi Schneur and Esty Perman.

4101503.name: Chabad of the Central West End
4101503.note: COLlive (29 Nov 2018, 'New Shluchim to S. Louis'): Rabbi Yossi and Goldie Abenson 'will be opening the first Chabad center in S. Louis, Missouri's, Central West End neighborhood'. Its chabad.org listing went up Aug 21 2018. St. Louis Jewish Light (4 April 2019): they 'recently established a Chabad center in the Central West End'. Jewish Light (11 Nov 2022): until then it 'operated from a home and rented office space'; from Nov 2022 a temporary space at Maryland and Euclid Avenues.

earlier.where: a home and rented office space

4108974.name: Chabad of Wichita & Rural Kansas
4108974.note: The Kansas City Jewish Chronicle (15 Nov 2018, 'Chabad opens new center in Wichita'): Rabbi Shmulik and Rebbetzin Chaya Mushka Greenberg 'moved to Wichita, Kansas, in August'; 'The Greenbergs opened the first Chabad Center in Wichita this August, just in time for' Rosh Hashanah. Its chabad.org listing went up Aug 16 2018. Later a centre at the Shops at Tallgrass (21st and Rock Road; date not found); now 251 S. Whittier Rd.

4486990.name: Chabad Jewish Center of St. Charles County
4486990.note: St. Louis Jewish Light (27 Dec 2019, 'Chabad launching chapter serving St. Charles'): 'On the first night of Hannukah [Dec 22 2019], the Chabad of Greater St. Louis announced a new fifth chapter serving St. Charles County', led by Rabbi Chaim and Bassy Landa. Its chabad.org listing went up Sept 17 2019. Now 119 S Main Street, St. Charles; a gift of 9.6 acres in O'Fallon for a future centre.

5116551.name: C-Teen
5116551.note: The Kansas City Jewish Chronicle (2 Sept 2021, 'Chabad rabbi and wife establish Cteen of KC'): Rabbi Avremi and Mushky Baron 'are establishing and directing Cteen of Kansas City', programming from early October; 'They recently moved to Leawood from Brooklyn'. Its chabad.org listing went up June 3 2021. KCteen's own centre opened in Feb 2023 on the Aspiria Campus (6450 Sprint Parkway) (KCJC, 5 April 2023).

6184697.name: JGrads
6184697.note: St. Louis Jewish Light (21 March 2008, 'JGrads helps connect students', reprinted on ChabadWashU.org; read in full): Michele Nudelman, a Washington University law and business student, 'and Rabbi Hershey Novack, who directs Washington University's Chabad on Campus, formed JGrads. Now in its third year, the organization spread throughout graduate school campuses in St. Louis' (so begun in the 2005-06 school year; medium). Since Dec 2023 it has its own shluchim: COLlive and Anash (22 Nov 2023): Rabbi Yankel and Chana Oster 'will arrive in St. Louis right before Chanukah to assume the directorship role of JGrads St. Louis. For the first time, there will be a dedicated shliach and shlucha'; St. Louis Jewish Light (23 Jan 2024).

6373098.name: The Friendship Circle of Kansas City
6373098.note: The Kansas City Jewish Chronicle (4 April 2024, 'The Friendship Circle of Kansas City launches debut program for children with disabilities'): Friends@Home, 'a program of Chabad of Kansas City', with Rabbi Avremi Baron. Its chabad.org listing went up March 21 2024.

6497961.name: Chabad Olathe
6497961.note: The Kansas City Jewish Chronicle (27 Feb 2025, 'New Chabad of Olathe brings city's first resident rabbi'): 'Rabbi Mendel Wenger and his wife, Sheina, arrived in late November' (2024), after several visits in 2024. Its chabad.org listing went up July 17 2024. CrownHeights.info (15 March 2025): 'The Wengers have moved to Olathe to establish its first-ever Jewish center'.

7285365.name: Chabad Jewish Center of Kirkwood
7285365.note: Rabbi Levi Kesselman. No founding source found yet (new); its chabad.org listing went up April 13 2026, so it existed by then.
